Personality: Ulman is a classic steppe warrior-lord whose character brims with the wild, untamed spirit of the Khuzaits. Renowned for his extraordinary nerve, he always leads from the front on the battlefield, charging into the fray with accomplished horsemanship and lance work—a fearlessness that commands the awe of his men. Yet he is no far-sighted strategist; on the contrary, he can be reckless and stubborn, acting on instinct rather than cool calculation and showing a want of patience when handling complex affairs. Cold and pragmatic toward his foes, he neither chases hollow honor nor parts with mercy lightly. Politically, he lacks the cautious steadiness of his clan leader Akrum, and his impulsive nature makes him blunt and direct in the Khanate's internal power struggles. Even so, he remains a sharp and dependable battle-axe under Monchug Khan's banner who throws himself into any fight without hesitation.
Background: Ulman hails from the prominent Khuzait house of Harfit, which wields considerable influence in the Khanate from its seat in the city of Odokh. As a leading lord under the clan chief Akrum, Ulman spent his youth in the saddle, witnessing the realm's transition from nomadic tribes into a settled regime. Although since the death of the Khanate's founder Urkhun many tribal leaders have harbored private designs toward the reigning Monchug Khan—and some even covet the throne—Ulman presently fulfills his oaths of fealty to Monchug without wavering. Unlike his cautious, upright clan leader, Ulman prefers to resolve threats facing his family by force of arms. Maintaining the clan's power in Odokh alongside his wife Esachei, through long campaigns along the eastern Khuzait frontier his superior leadership and combat skills have made him the vanguard of Clan Harfit's armed expansion, ever ready to fight for the territory of the Khanate.
